message.content:
Below are two ways you can spin up a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU (if it’s available in your region) and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
(If the RTX A6000 isn’t offered in your zone, you’ll need to pick another GPU type such as `NVIDIA_TESLA_A100`.)

---

## 1. `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # adjust CPU/RAM as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="NVIDIA_TESLA_A6000" # change if unavailable
DISK_SIZE_GB=100
DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size="$DISK_SIZE_GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="$DISK_TYPE" \
  --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional
```

> **Notes**
> * Make sure the **Compute Engine API** is enabled and you have a **billing account** attached to the project.
> * Verify that the chosen zone actually offers the `NVIDIA_TESLA_A6000` GPU. Run `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE` to see available types.
> * The `startup.sh` script is optional – you can use it to install drivers or run custom commands after boot.

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

```json
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/NVIDIA_TESLA_A6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **How to call it**
> 1. Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
> 2. Authenticate with OAuth 2.0 (e.g., `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`) and include the token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.  
> 3. Send the request via `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client.

---

### Quick sanity check

```bash
# List available GPU types in a zone
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=us-central1-a
```

If `NVIDIA_TESLA_A6000` is missing, switch to a supported type like `NVIDIA_TESLA_A100`.

---

**That’s it!** Once the instance is running, you’ll have an Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for your workloads.
